q: 1. Which of the following is a dummy activity?
options: Await the arrival of concrete material
explain: Per the answer key, b.

q: 2. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float is defined as the difference between total float and free float of an activity.

q: 3. The time by which the completion of an activity can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities is called
explain: That is the definition of free float.

q: 4. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The activity which consumes maximum time, is called a node
The activity is the time consuming part of a project
The beginning and end of a job, are called events
Logically and sequentially connected activities and events form a network
explain: This statement is incorrect - a 'node' represents an event (start/end point), not the activity consuming maximum time.

q: 5. Fulkerson's rule is used for numbering the
explain: Fulkerson's rule numbers the events so that each head number exceeds its tail number.

q: 6. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities, is known as:
explain: Free float specifically measures delay possible in an activity without affecting the succeeding activity's start.

q: 7. In a PERT network, the earliest (activity) start time is the
options: Earliest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
Latest time that an activity can be started without delaying the entire project.
Earliest time that an activity can start without violation of precedence requirements.
Latest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
explain: Earliest start time is defined as the earliest possible time an activity can begin, respecting all preceding activity dependencies.

q: 8. Which of the following is one of the assumptions of PERT?
options: Total project completion time follows a normal probability distribution.
Activity times are dependent and correlated.
Project completion time follows a skewed chi-square distribution.
Activity times are known with certainty.
explain: PERT assumes that the sum of many independent activity durations along the critical path leads to an overall project completion time following a normal distribution (by central limit theorem).

q: 9. A construction schedule is prepared after collecting
explain: Scheduling requires comprehensive data on task quantities, labor productivity (output), and machinery capacity to determine durations.

q: 10. An important assumption in PERT calculations is:
explain: PERT assumes individual activity times are statistically independent of each other, which allows summing their variances along the critical path.

q: 11. Construction site planning is mainly depends upon the
explain: Effective site layout and planning must account for the type of project, the physical constraints of the site, and how the work will be performed.

q: 12. Which is/are features of PERT/CPM?
options: An estimate of how long a project will take.
A graphical display of project activities.
explain: PERT/CPM techniques provide time estimates, graphical network displays, and identify critical activities - all of the above.

q: 13. An event is indicated on the network by a number enclosed in
explain: Events are conventionally represented on network diagrams by numbers enclosed within circles (nodes).

q: 14. In the given figure, the network of a project represents
options: activity of an excavation of a footing
activity of an excavation which starts at event No. 1 and ends at even No. 2
activity of excavation which takes 8 units of time
explain: The figure shows the excavation activity between events 1 and 2 labeled with duration '8', indicating it takes 8 units of time to complete.

q: 15. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: The completion point of an activity is called an event, represented as a node/connector point - all the above terms apply.

q: 16. If for a activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is ? days then the expected time is
explain: The most likely time is cut off in the scan. The key answer 3.5 follows from tE = (1 + 4m + 8)/6 with m = 3 days.

q: 17. Standard deviation when optimistic time and earliest expected time
explain: The stem is incomplete in the book. Using the previous question's data, σ = (8 – 1)/6 = 1.167 days.

q: 18. A Milestone chart
options: shows the interdependencies of various jobs
depicts the delay of jobs, if any
points outgoing ahead of schedule of jobs, if any
explain: A milestone chart does not show interdependencies between jobs (that's a network diagram's function), so per the answer key, none of these accurately describes it fully.

q: 19. Slack is
options: difference of lastest allowable time and earliest expected time
earliest expected time - lastest allowable time
explain: Slack = latest allowable time – earliest expected time.

q: 20. The total cost verses time curve of an activity is
explain: Combining decreasing indirect costs and increasing direct costs yields a distinct U-shaped total cost curve with a clear minimum cost point.

q: 21. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: in a network activities are represented by arrows and events are circled
events into which a number of activities enter and from which one or several activities emerge are called the merge nodes
events into which one or several activities enter and from which a number of emerging activities are generated are called burst nodes
explain: All three statements are correct, so d.

q: 22. In the initial stage of the project the probability of completing the project is
explain: At the initial stage of a project, uncertainty is highest and progress is minimal, so the probability of on-time completion assessment tends to be low.

q: 23. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float = total float – free float.

q: 24. Negative float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Negative float means super-critical.

q: 25. The process of incorporating changes and rescheduling or replanning is called
explain: Updating is the process of incorporating changes and rescheduling/replanning the project based on actual progress.

q: 26. Zero float any activity means that the activity is
explain: Zero float means critical.

q: 27. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is
explain: Positive float means sub-critical.

q: 28. The total float for any activity along the critical path in CPM is
explain: Critical activities have zero total float.

q: 29. Choose the correct statement from the following:
explain: PERT is indeed event-oriented, making this the correct statement among the options.

q: 30. Project control begins early in the project with planning and ends late in the project with
explain: Project control spans from early planning through to a final post-implementation review at project closeout.

q: 31. Identify the man out
explain: 'Design completed' is an event; the others are activities.

q: 32. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities is known as:
explain: Free float specifically defines the permissible delay in an activity that does not affect the succeeding activity's start time.

q: 33. An important principle in drawing a network is
options: no activity can start until all the previous activities in the same chain are completed
parallel activities should begin and end at the same time
between two events there should not be more than two activities
the number of dummy activities in a network should not exceed 4
has no bearing on the network and appear anywhere
explain: The precedence rule: an activity starts only after all its predecessors finish.

q: 34. If the scheduled completion time of a project is more than the earliest expected time for completion of the project, then the probability of completion of the project within the scheduled completion time will be
explain: If the scheduled time exceeds the expected (mean) time, the project has a higher-than-average chance of completion within schedule, i.e., more than 50%.

q: 35. A dummy activity
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: A dummy consumes no time or resources.

q: 36. At an event other than final event if no activity emerges, it results in an error called
explain: An event with no outgoing activity is a dangling error.

q: 37. Aggregate planning is planning for
explain: Aggregate planning looks at the total capacity and resource needs for the entire project rather than individual small tasks.

q: 38. Critical path moves along the activities having total float?
explain: By definition, the critical path consists of activities with zero total float.

q: 39. Negative slack occurs
options: when lastest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events sticks to their schedule
explain: Per the answer key, c. Negative slack arises when the schedule is behind, which needs extra resources.

q: 40. Critical path
explain: The critical path has the minimum slack (zero or negative).

q: 41. The objective of technical planning is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
taking remedial action about bottle-neck in execution
explain: Technical planning covers the entire lifecycle from setting standards to resource management and problem-solving during execution.

q: 42. Float is
options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
lastest time by which an activity can be delayed without hapering the completion of the project
lastest allowable time - earliest expected time
time available time required for an activity
explain: Per the answer key, d: float is the time available minus the time required.

q: 43. For the execution of work in time, work plan is prepared by
explain: The contractor is responsible for creating the detailed schedule and work plan to ensure they meet the contractual deadlines.

q: 44. Which one is the basis of project?
explain: A project is built on the pillars of planning what to do, scheduling when to do it, and monitoring to ensure it is done correctly.

q: 45. In PERT (Programme Evaluation & Review Technique) analysis the duration of the activities is taken as:
explain: PERT uses the expected mean time (calculated from the three time estimates) as the duration for scheduling calculations.

q: 46. Latest starts of an activity is always
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event tie of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: Per the answer key, a.

q: 47. 'Wait' in PERT, belongs to the category of
explain: Waiting takes time, so it is an activity.

q: 48. An activity of the project is graphically represented by ……… on the network.
explain: Activities are arrows; events are circles.

q: 49. Which of the following statement is correct about the network diagram?
options: The events are represented graphically by circles or nodes at the beginning and the end of activity by arrows.
The tail end of the arrow represents the start of the activity
The head of the arrow represents the end of an activity
explain: All three are correct.

q: 50. Which operation must complete first?
options: Right of the line joining two circles
Left of the line joining two circle
explain: The operation on the left (the predecessor) completes first.
